turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey Marcus, you got a sec? I need to vent about the DNS switch last week.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh no, what happened? I saw the incident ticket — looked rough.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Rough is an understatement. I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was actually ready. I thought the provisioning was done, but the health checks weren't even passing.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yikes. So traffic hit a cluster that couldn't serve it?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. Every region went down — the outage lasted for hours. Customers were not happy, and neither was my manager.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's brutal. What's the fix going forward?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I'm going to be way more careful. This time, I waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS — I literally sat there refreshing the status page until it was green. Then I flipped the record.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So you're doing it manually but with a checklist?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, for now. It worked — traffic moved over without a hitch. But I know I'm one tired day away from repeating the same mistake.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw you pushed a new DNS config. Looks like you added some automation?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I set up health-check-gated DNS failover. So if the cluster goes unhealthy, traffic auto-routes away from it. No more manual waiting.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice, that's a solid upgrade. But I also heard you had a schema migration issue last week?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Ugh, don't remind me. I migrated the schema without a backup — I thought, 'it's just adding a column, what could go wrong?'

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The migration corrupted customer records. We had to restore from a nightly snapshot, but we lost a few hours of data. It was a mess.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Ouch. So what are you doing differently now?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I took a full snapshot before the migration this time — and I tested the rollback path. The migration could always be rolled back now, which is a huge relief.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. Learning from pain, I guess.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, but I still feel like I'm patching things one at a time.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, you look like you've been staring at the DNS dashboard for hours. Everything okay?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Honestly? No. I had a wake-up call this morning. We had a minor blip on the new cluster — nothing big, but the health check went red for like 30 seconds.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: But you have the failover now, right? It should have auto-routed.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It did — but only because I had set it up. The problem is, I realized that my earlier approach — waiting for the cluster health check before switching DNS — turns out that wasn't enough. It was still a manual step, and I was the only one who could do it. If I'm on vacation or asleep, nobody else would know to wait.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So you're saying the manual wait was the weak link?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about thinking 'I'll just be careful' would solve it. So I replaced the manual wait with fully automated health-check-gated DNS — no human can skip the wait anymore. The system checks, and if it's not healthy, it won't even attempt to switch.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a big step. So no more 'Priya has to remember to check'?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Right. The automation is the gatekeeper now. I can't override it even if I wanted to — which is exactly what I need, because my judgment clearly failed me before.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Well, at least you're not relying on yourself anymore. That's progress.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah. It took two outages and a near-miss to get here, but I think this is finally the right design.
